# omx-dsp

omx-dsp is the DSP library of the FreeMixer/OpenMixer console, in plain C11. It holds the filters, one-pole smoothers, delay lines, sample-rate converter, MIDI note map and effect kernels, with the instance faces through which the mixing engine and the omx plugins drive them. [FreeMixer/omx-dsp](https://github.com/FreeMixer/omx-dsp) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for omx-dsp

**Status: available.** Of omx-dsp's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 6 of 6. 24 binaries, 10 MB. 48 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 48 open.

Built from omx-dsp 0.27.0 (commit `a0ee1dfe`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_fx](fuzz_fx/) | Picks one of the 25 effect instance faces from the first byte, then a rate from the oracle grid or any rate from 8 to 768 kHz. It creates two instances at that rate. For up to eight steps it reads a bypass bit, the face's control ports as raw float or int words (NaN and infinities included), a block length of 1 to 512 frames and two channels of samples (finite at a chosen loudness, or any float word in hostile mode). Both instances get the same ports; one runs the block in place and the other out of place. | 5 checks (api-contract, differential, invariant, self-validation; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7 |
| [fuzz_laws](fuzz_laws/) | Reads up to 64 calls, each picked by a selector byte. Its arguments are raw float words where a law takes any value, two-byte values mapped onto a law's travel, selector bytes (block lengths, pan leg, rate) and single bits (mutes). The calls cover the clamps and unit knob, dB to linear and back in both forms, the pan and balance laws, the fader coefficient, the linear ramp, the wet/dry mix and cross-fade, and the one-pole constructors, rescale and step. Each result is checked against its law, and the contract ledger is read after each call. | 9 checks (algebraic, invariant, roundtrip, self-validation; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9 |
| [fuzz_eq](fuzz_eq/) | Reads a rate (from the oracle grid or any rate from 8 to 768 kHz) and designs the head high-pass and low-pass from raw double corners. It then reads 1 to 24 bands, each with a kind, an on switch, a raw double corner and Q, and a gain within +-24 dB or exactly 0, and designs the bank. It evaluates the bank's magnitude at four frequencies, runs a finite block of 1 to 255 samples through the mono or stereo cascade, and calls the two bandwidth-to-Q conversions. | 8 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, self-validation; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9 |
| [fuzz_src](fuzz_src/) | Reads a source and destination rate as any 32-bit words and asks for a conversion plan; when the plan is refused, the run ends there. Otherwise it designs the polyphase table and reads up to 16 blocks of finite samples, 0 to 512 each. It converts the take twice: once in a single call, and once either whole or cut into the blocks the input gave, with or without a final flush. The two outputs, the plan and the table are then checked. | 8 checks (algebraic, api-contract, differential, invariant, reference-oracle, self-validation; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7 |
| [fuzz_delay](fuzz_delay/) | Reads a flags byte and a ring size of 1 to 4096. The fractional mode arms a Lagrange delay line of order 3, order 5 or any signed byte, and runs up to 12 finite blocks, each with any float delay. The integer mode runs up to 12 blocks of a stereo or mono integer delay pair, with delays in tenths of a millisecond at a declared rate. It can also check the ms-to-samples conversion for any finite ms and rate. The harness keeps its own copy of the take as the oracle. | 10 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, self-validation; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7 |
| [fuzz_note_map](fuzz_note_map/) | Builds a valid note leg (channel, key range, transpose, velocity curve, fixed velocity) from six bytes. It then runs records until the input ends: three raw MIDI bytes through the map, a set_leg with six raw ints (or a valid leg from bytes), or a release_all with a cap of 1 to 4. A model of the downstream synth's sounding notes, the harness's own copy of the leg in force and its own table of held keys check each output. At the end it releases everything and checks every velocity curve. | 9 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, self-validation; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9 |

## What the statements say, for omx-dsp
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch omx-dsp
    ./oft verify-sha omx-dsp

By hand: download `omx-dsp-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/omx-dsp/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeMixer/omx-dsp](https://github.com/FreeMixer/omx-dsp) at `a0ee1dfeefff63c25bf37e95d31683ec12c0f690` (0.27.0), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/omx-dsp` at `e50b6f9cb4bf28b71ec22ad478d23f15406164f5` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`omx-dsp-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `omx-dsp-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).
